svg.title: Money-to-Manpower Score
svg.desc: candidate number: 5; slug: unclaimed-property-recovery; title: Unclaimed Property Recovery; category: Recovery services; production stage: approved_master; scores: revenue potential: 20; profit margin potential: 22; team efficiency: 18; startup accessibility: 13; automation potential: 12; dimension max: revenue potential: 25; profit margin potential: 25; team efficiency: 20; startup accessibility: 15; automation potential: 15; total score: 85; tier label: Elite Small-Team Cash Machine; evidence confidence: High; uncertainty band: ±3 pts; uncertainty bounds: low: 82; high: 88; uncertainty note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.; score rationale: revenue potential: Revenue Potential: 20/25. Low-capital research scales moderately; free state claims constrain pricing.; profit margin potential: Profit Margin Potential: 22/25. Low-capital research scales moderately; free state claims constrain pricing.; team efficiency: Team Efficiency: 18/20. Low-capital research scales moderately; free state claims constrain pricing.; startup accessibility: Startup Accessibility: 13/15. Low-capital research scales moderately; free state claims constrain pricing.; automation potential: Automation Potential: 12/15. Low-capital research scales moderately; free state claims constrain pricing.; economics: gross revenue range: $60,000–$450,000 USD annually; net profit margin range: 25–50%; owner net profit potential: $15,000–$225,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $5,000–$35,000 USD; monthly opex range: $1,500–$8,000 USD; time to first deal: 3–12 months; typical team size: full time including owner: 1; contractors: 2; total people: 3; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Recognized service fees, not client asset value; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.; estimate status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data; scenarios: conservative: annual gross revenue usd: 60000; net profit margin pct: 25; annual owner net profit usd: 15000; full time including owner: 1; contractors: 2; total people: 3; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; base case: annual gross revenue usd: 255000.0; net profit margin pct: 37.5; annual owner net profit usd: 95625; full time including owner: 1; contractors: 2; total people: 3; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; scaled small team: annual gross revenue usd: 450000; net profit margin pct: 50; annual owner net profit usd: 225000; full time including owner: 2; contractors: 3; total people: 5; assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.; automation levers: Record matching; Claim status tracking; key risks: Identity mismatch; Low claim values; Customer distrust; regulatory notes: Check finder registration, fee caps, waiting periods and privacy obligations.; Disclose the owner's ability to claim directly without a recovery service.; track ids: track_1; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; plays: id: public_record_api_intelligence; track id: track_1; name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.; inputs: Court & probate dockets; State controller ledgers; Public licensing & entity APIs; workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence; Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold; Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution; metrics: Cost per verified lead; Docket-to-contact latency (hours); Net recovery / conversion rate; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; id: distressed_asset_recovery; track id: track_1; name: Distressed Asset Recovery; mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.; inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers; Unclaimed property & judgment dockets; Surplus auction manifests; workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances; Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value; Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts; metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case; Claim approval rate; Days from filing to disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold; trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules; impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle; detection metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance; fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required; id: b2b_class_action_contingency_recovery; track id: track_1; name: B2B Class-Action & Antitrust Settlement Contingency Recovery; mechanism: Monitor multibillion-dollar corporate antitrust and commercial class-action settlement funds (payment-card interchange, freight, auto parts, commercial insurance, SaaS) where 85–90% of eligible small businesses never file, and recover verified payouts on a 25–33% contingency fee.; inputs: Active federal B2B class-action settlement docket calendar & claims-administrator portals; B2B merchant-processing, fleet, & vendor spend intake pipeline; Contingency claim-preparation & court-authorized third-party filing agreements; workflow: Track open and upcoming commercial class-action settlements with verified court-appointed claims administrators and $50M–$5B+ settlement pools; Sign zero-upfront-cost (25–33% contingency) authorization agreements with operating restaurants, medical practices, retailers, and fleets; Extract historical merchant statements or vendor invoices, submit audited claim packages to the settlement administrator, and reconcile fee splits upon disbursement; metrics: Average gross settlement recovery per enrolled business ($5,000–$150,000+); Claim acceptance rate by court-appointed administrator (%); Net contingency fee per operator hour invested; platform risks: failure mode: Claim rejection, administrator audit hold, or court cap on third-party filer fees; trigger: Submitting unsubstantiated spend estimates, missing court bar dates, or failing to include required third-party filer disclosures; impact: Delayed payout disbursement or court-mandated fee reduction; detection metric: Deficiency-notice rate (<2% target) and 100% court-approved disclosure compliance; fallback: File strictly for verified operating businesses with primary processor/vendor statements and use court-approved third-party claim-filing riders; id: unclaimed_property_escheatment_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery; mechanism: Ingest state controller/treasury escheatment ledgers and uncashed municipal/corporate warrant registries above $25,000, cross-match corporate officers via Secretary of State filings, and execute statutory recovery agreements for a 10–25% contingent finder fee.; inputs: State controller/treasury escheatment bulk ledgers; Uncashed municipal warrant & vendor-credit registries; Secretary of State officer & FEIN cross-match index; workflow: Filter state unclaimed-property and uncashed-warrant ledgers for high-value corporate and estate accounts exceeding $25,000; Resolve active corporate officers, successor entities, or authorized fiduciaries via SOS and skip-trace databases; Execute state-compliant finder agreements with statutory fee caps and submit notarized claim packages to the treasury administrator; metrics: Average gross warrant/escheatment claim size ($25k+); Treasury claim approval rate (%); Days from notarized filing to state disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory finder-fee cap violation or waiting-period rejection; trigger: Charging above state statutory fee limits (e.g., 10% in CA/FL/NY) or soliciting claims during restricted post-escheatment windows; impact: Voided recovery contract, state controller rejection, or administrative penalty; detection metric: State-by-state fee-cap compliance check (100% pass) and claim rejection notice rate; fallback: Enforce per-state statutory fee caps and waiting-period rules in intake templates and disclose the owner's right to claim directly for free; id: freight_detention_audit_contingency; track id: track_1; name: Automated Parcel, LTL Freight & Tariff Overcharge Contingency Auditing; mechanism: Ingest mid-market shippers' UPS/FedEx/LTL EDI billing feeds and CBP Form 7501 customs entry summaries via read-only API to programmatically flag late-delivery SLA refunds, dimensional-weight billing errors, and duty-drawback refunds on a 35–50% contingency split.; inputs: Read-only UPS/FedEx/LTL carrier billing API & EDI 210 feeds; CBP ACE Form 7501 customs entry & HTS tariff schedules; Automated carrier dispute & duty-drawback claim submission engine; workflow: Connect read-only to shipper parcel/freight portals and ingest historical and daily invoice line items; Flag guaranteed-service late deliveries, duplicate accessorial fees, residential surcharges, and eligible export duty drawbacks; Auto-file carrier credit disputes and customs drawback claims, billing the client strictly 35–50% of verified credits posted to their statement; metrics: Recovered credits as % of total annual parcel/freight spend (2–8% target); Dispute acceptance rate by carrier/customs (%); Monthly recurring contingency revenue per shipper account; platform risks: failure mode: Carrier anti-automation lockouts or GSR (Guaranteed Service Refund) waiver clauses; trigger: Carriers inserting GSR waiver riders into custom shipper pricing agreements or throttling automated dispute bots; impact: Reduction in late-delivery refund volume on waived accounts; detection metric: Claim approval ratio per carrier and % of audit recovery derived from billing/dim-weight errors vs. GSR; fallback: Pivot audit rules toward non-waivable dimensional-weight, duplicate-charge, LTL freight class, and contract-rate benchmarking recoveries; id: hospital_lien_medical_receivables_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Out-of-Network Medical Claim & ERISA Appeal Contingency Recovery; mechanism: Partner with surgical centers, air/ground ambulance operators, and specialty clinics to ingest underpaid or denied commercial insurance claims, automating federal No Surprises Act IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) and ERISA administrative appeals on a 20–35% contingency fee.; inputs: Provider 835/837 EDI remittance & denial feeds (CO-45, CO-50, PR-96 codes); Qualified Payment Amount (QPA) & regional FAIR Health benchmark database; Automated ERISA plan-document demand & Federal IDR portal filing workflow; workflow: Ingest denied and severely underpaid out-of-network commercial claims from specialty medical practices; Cross-reference payer remittances against statutory Open Negotiation windows (30 business days) under the No Surprises Act and ERISA SPD timelines; Generate evidence-backed arbitration briefs and ERISA appeals, collecting 20–35% of the incremental insurer payout above the initial remittance; metrics: Average incremental recovery per arbitrated claim ($1,500–$25,000+); IDR / ERISA appeal win rate vs. initial payer offer (%); Contingency revenue per practice partner per month; platform risks: failure mode: Missed 30-day Open Negotiation / 4-day IDR initiation statutory deadlines or HIPAA breach; trigger: Failing to file within strict federal No Surprises Act business-day windows or handling PHI without a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA); impact: Permanent forfeiture of IDR arbitration eligibility on expired claims or HIPAA compliance penalties; detection metric: 100% BAA execution before EDI ingestion and automated T-minus-5-day statutory deadline alerts; fallback: Enforce HIPAA-compliant encrypted EDI pipelines with signed BAAs and fall back to longer-window ERISA administrative appeals when IDR windows have lapsed; id: property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency; track id: track_1; name: Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage; mechanism: Ingest county tax-assessor valuation rolls upon annual notice release, run an automated valuation model (AVM) flagging parcels assessed above comparable neighbor equity ratios, and file bulk administrative tax protests for 30–50% of the first year's verified tax reduction.; inputs: Annual county tax-assessor preliminary valuation rolls & parcel GIS characteristics; Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine; Bulk administrative ARB (Appraisal Review Board) protest filing & hearing pipeline; workflow: Ingest county assessment rolls the day annual valuation notices drop and compute each parcel's assessed-per-sqft percentile against direct neighborhood peers; Mail personalized pre-filled protest postcards showing the owner's exact estimated over-assessment and a QR code to sign a zero-upfront-cost contingency authorization; Auto-generate uniform comparable-equity evidence packets, file bulk administrative protests before the county bar date, and collect 30–50% of Year-1 tax savings; metrics: Protest-window mail-to-signed-authorization conversion %; Percentage of appealed parcels receiving an assessment reduction (65–85% target); Average net contingency fee per residential ($150–$450) and commercial ($2,000–$15,000) parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State property-tax consultant licensing requirements or missed county protest bar dates; trigger: Representing property owners for a fee without required state registration (e.g., Texas TDLR Property Tax Consultant license) or missing the 30/45-day county filing deadline; impact: Rejected bulk filings, administrative fines, or zero contingency revenue for the tax year; detection metric: 100% licensed tax-agent sign-off in regulated states and T-minus-7-day bulk filing completion; fallback: Partner with licensed local property-tax consultants/attorneys of record in regulated states and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing; id: transferable_tax_credit_brokerage_syndication; track id: track_1; name: Transferable Federal & State Tax Credit Brokerage & Syndication (IRA § 6418 / Film / Historic); mechanism: Scraping federal DOE/EPA interconnection queues, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries to originate transferable tax credits (IRC § 6418 Clean Energy Investment/Production Credits, Georgia/Louisiana Film Credits, State Historic Rehab & Brownfield Credits) from cash-strapped project developers at $0.82–$0.88 on the dollar and flipping them in simultaneous escrow closings to corporate and HNW taxpayers at $0.92–$0.96 on the dollar.; inputs: State film-office production certifications, National Park Service Part 2/3 Historic Preservation filings, and utility solar/biogas/storage interconnection queues; IRS Energy Credits Online pre-filing registration verification and tax-credit recapture insurance underwriting partners; Outbound network of CPA managing partners, corporate tax directors, and family-office CIOs with $1M–$50M+ in quarterly federal/state tax liabilities; workflow: Monitor public project registries to identify middle-market solar, RNG, battery storage, independent film, and historic-rehab developers holding $1M–$25M in newly generated transferable credits; Lock up exclusive purchase or placement options at $0.83–$0.89 per $1.00 of credit prior to quarterly corporate estimated tax deadlines (April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Dec 15); Package the credits with a third-party CPA cost-segregation/eligibility opinion and tax-credit recapture insurance policy; Execute a simultaneous bilateral escrow closing with a corporate taxpayer at $0.92–$0.95 on the dollar—saving the buyer 5–8% guaranteed on their tax bill while capturing a 400–800 bps riskless spread ($40k–$80k per $1M block); metrics: Face value of tax credits placed per quarter ($5M–$100M+); Net retained principal/brokerage spread (400–800 bps) per closed tranche; Days in escrow from developer IRS registration number issuance to wire settlement; platform risks: failure mode: IRS § 6418 recapture event or state department-of-revenue basis challenge; trigger: Project developer inflating eligible cost basis or taking a clean-energy asset out of service during the 5-year recapture window; impact: Taxpayer recapture assessment plus penalties if uninsured; detection metric: 100% independent Big-4/national CPA cost-basis audit and mandatory A-rated tax-credit recapture insurance binder on every tranche; fallback: Never take unhedged balance-sheet inventory risk; close strictly via simultaneous back-to-back escrow funded by the buyer's wire and backed by non-cancelable tax-credit insurance; id: chapter11_trade_claim_convenience_class_rollup; track id: track_1; name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups; mechanism: Purchase documented small trade claims below risk-adjusted expected plan distributions, accounting for objections, assignment procedures, and plan rules that may prohibit claim splitting or aggregation benefits.; inputs: Bankruptcy schedules E/F and claims register; Invoices, payment history, and assignment documents; Proposed plan classification and distribution waterfall; workflow: 1. Reconcile scheduled trade creditors with filed claims and supporting invoices; 2. Model recoveries under plan amendments, objections, setoffs, and convenience-class eligibility; 3. Buy eligible claims through documented assignments and complete required transfer notices; 4. Monitor objections and confirmation, then reconcile distributions to each acquired claim; metrics: Purchase discount to risk-adjusted recovery; Allowed claim value versus purchased face value; Realized return and days to distribution; platform risks: failure mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion; trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims; impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss; detection metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio; fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries; id: out_of_statute_zombie_debt_portfolio_settlement; track id: track_1; name: Out-of-Statute Charged-Off Debt Portfolio & Self-Serve Tradeline Settlement Funnels; mechanism: Evaluate heavily discounted time-barred receivables for lawful voluntary resolution, separating collection limitation periods from credit-reporting limits and excluding extinguished or otherwise uncollectible obligations.; inputs: Account-level ownership and payment history; State limitation, revival, and collection-disclosure matrix; Dispute records and credit-reporting eligibility dates; workflow: 1. Validate account ownership, balances, bankruptcy status, and applicable limitation periods; 2. Obtain licensed legal review of collectibility, required notices, and payment-revival consequences; 3. Offer permitted voluntary self-service resolutions without lawsuit threats or credit-deletion promises; 4. Honor disputes and opt-outs, issue satisfaction records, and update only accurate eligible reporting; metrics: Validated legally collectible balance share; Net voluntary receipts after servicing costs; Dispute and disclosure-defect rate; platform risks: failure mode: Time-barred collection or reporting violation; trigger: Threatened litigation, unlawful revival solicitation, or re-aging of obsolete debt; impact: Enforcement, restitution, and servicing suspension; detection metric: Accounts failing legal-age checks and substantiated complaints; fallback: Suppress affected accounts, correct reporting, and suspend collection until counsel approves remediation; id: state_film_historic_brownfield_tax_credit_brokerage; track id: track_1; name: State Film, Historic Rehabilitation (HTC) & Brownfield Transferable Tax Credit Placement; mechanism: Match certified state film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield credits with eligible taxpayers at negotiated discounts, retaining disclosed placement fees; transferability and buyer usability are state-specific and do not imply federal historic credits can be sold outright.; inputs: State agency project approvals and issued credit certificates; Transfer rules, recapture terms, and seller ownership records; Buyer state tax liabilities and escrow placement agreements; workflow: 1. Identify certified credits and verify state-specific transferability, issuance status, and remaining carryforward life; 2. Have independent advisers validate eligible costs, ownership, liens, recapture exposure, and buyer utilization limits; 3. Match approved buyers and sellers with disclosed pricing, fees, indemnities, and any available insurance exclusions; 4. Complete required agency transfer approvals and escrow settlement, then retain filing and post-close monitoring records; metrics: Certified transferable credit face value placed; Net placement fee per settled transaction; Transfer approval and escrow cycle days; platform risks: failure mode: Transfer rejected or purchased credit unusable; trigger: State rule change, certificate defect, recapture event, or buyer liability mismatch; impact: Failed closing or buyer tax shortfall and indemnity dispute; detection metric: Unresolved certificate exceptions and buyer utilization coverage; fallback: Suspend settlement under diligence contingencies and rematch only verified eligible credits without guaranteeing tax savings; id: wotc_hourly_payroll_tax_credit_contingency_engine; track id: track_1; name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine; mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.; inputs: Consented hiring records, Form 8850 responses, and payroll hours; Research project evidence and qualified expense ledgers; State workforce certification procedures and tax-year credit and fee rules; workflow: 1. Confirm WOTC authorization for each hire date and complete required prescreening by the job-offer date; 2. Submit Form 8850 and required supporting forms within the applicable 28-day deadline and track state certification and qualifying hours; 3. Separately document Section 41 qualifying research and expenses, reconciling wage overlap and applicable deduction adjustments with a tax professional; 4. Obtain employer and preparer approval before filing, retain audit support, and collect permitted fees without guaranteeing credits; metrics: Timely WOTC certification submission rate; Substantiated credits realized by the employer; Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs; platform risks: failure mode: Credit denial or impermissible contingent-fee arrangement; trigger: Expired program authority, late certification, unsupported research expenses, or restricted practitioner compensation; impact: Reduced credits, amended returns, penalties, and fee repayment exposure; detection metric: Deadline exceptions, certification denials, and unsupported expense share; fallback: Exclude unsupported claims and use compliant fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; play id: public_record_api_intelligence; text.title: gross revenue range: $60,000–$450,000 USD annually; net profit margin range: 25–50%; owner net profit potential: $15,000–$225,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment; startup capital range: $5,000–$35,000 USD; monthly opex range: $1,500–$8,000 USD; time to first deal: 3–12 months; typical team size: full time including owner: 1; contractors: 2; total people: 3; includes contractors note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.; revenue basis: Recognized service fees, not client asset value; cost basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.; estimate status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data
